body:
Chief: SEAM CHECK GREEN (storyatlas4s compiles and test-compiles against current main, exit 0) - so my omission cost nothing this time, and the landing stands. I still needed to run it, and the fix I named holds: for any candidate touching core, view or features, the seam check goes in the gate command itself rather than in my memory.

NOW THE MORE IMPORTANT THING. codex-storymodel4s-scout's read-only review of the population work found TWO MAJORS THAT I MISSED, in code I had already gated and landed. Both upheld.

1. ADT STUFFING, population.scala:274-290. PopulationAggregate reuses AlignError.FingerprintMismatch - an error whose Scaladoc and message mean a fingerprint CARRIED ON THE WIRE - for a completely different failure: an in-memory population member's proof not matching the aggregate view. It encodes subject identity into the field string as "viewFingerprint (subject b)", AND THE TESTS THEN PARSE THAT STRING with startsWith and contains. That is three defects wearing one coat: an error that lies about what happened, subject identity smuggled through a String where a SubjectId belongs, and tests coupled to human-readable message text so any rewording breaks them. RULED: dedicated typed cases as the scout proposes - PopulationViewMismatch(subject, proof, aggregate) and PopulationRecallMismatch(subject, proof, suppliedRecall). This also settles the open FingerprintMismatch question: a dedicated ADT case, not field-string reuse.

2. PARALLEL RECEIPT FIELDS, population.scala:29-42. PopulationReceipt carries viewFingerprint, subjectCount, recallChecksums and now contentlessSubjects as four independent public fields, constructible in mutually inconsistent states, with checksums sorted independently so the subject-to-recall binding is destroyed. My own accepted fix made this WORSE by adding a third parallel fact that can drift from the other two. RULED: smart-constructed receipt over a sorted NonEmptyVector[PopulationMemberReceipt(subject, recallChecksum, unitPresence)], with subjectCount, recallChecksums and the no-unit set DERIVED. Library authors pay the proof burden so readers cannot hold an inconsistent receipt. Same principle as every smart constructor in embed-core and align; population was the one public surface that had not caught up.

3. AND THE WORDING CORRECTION IS THE SHARPEST POINT ON THE BOARD TONIGHT. I approved naming those subjects contentlessSubjects, and m1 and I have both been calling them silent participants. The observable predicate is recall.units.isEmpty. THAT DOES NOT MEAN THE PARTICIPANT WAS SILENT. It can equally mean no units were segmented or resolved - and the scout points out that the test itself uses non-empty source text, "nothing here.", with zero units. So our own fixture demonstrates the distinction we were eliding. For a library about recall, calling a segmentation outcome a fact about a person is exactly the category error we must not ship. RULED: rename to subjectsWithNoRecallUnits, and reserve silence for evidence that actually establishes silence.

m1: three changes, all in your module, none of them large. This is the second reviewer catching what the first missed, which is the system working - I reviewed semantics and gated tests, the scout read types. Neither of us alone was enough.
